title: Activity-induced emergent flatness, instabilities and pattern formation in fluid membranes
authors: Debayan Jana, Astik Haldar, Abhik Basu
abstract: We show that microscopically inversion-asymmetric, permeable active fluid membranes are statistically flat and effectively inversion-symmetric at large scales. Their fluctuations are governed by an asymptotically exact linear hydrodynamic equation giving orientational long-range order and positional quasi-long-range order. At intermediate scales, their dynamics is described by a Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation with spatially long-range noise, producing rough membranes with short-range translational and long-range orientational order described by exactly known scaling exponents. Active stresses can destabilize the membrane at long wavelengths, while sufficiently strong active permeation flow can drive finite-wavevector instabilities and pattern formation. These results reveal a novel activity-driven route to the destruction of flat fluid membranes.
summary: This paper analyzes the complex dynamics of active fluid membranes, showing how they achieve emergent symmetry at large scales while exhibiting rich pattern formation at intermediate length scales. The dynamics are governed by a modified hydrodynamic equation, which predicts instabilities driven by active stresses. The work details how nonlinearity can stabilize or destroy these patterned states depending on its magnitude.
main_problem: The study investigates the non-equilibrium dynamics, emergent symmetries, instabilities, and pattern formation in active fluid membranes.
main_result: The membrane exhibits emergent flatness and quasi-long-range order at large scales, but active stresses can induce instabilities leading to pattern formation at intermediate scales.
method: The analysis employs hydrodynamic theory, Renormalization Group (RG) techniques, and linear stability analysis applied to the height field equation.
model_or_system: The system is a nearly flat, inversion-asymmetric, permeable active fluid membrane embedded in a 3D bulk isotropic fluid, modeled by a height field $h(x, t)$.
key_observables: Height fluctuations $\langle(\delta h)^2angle$, scaling exponents ($\chi, 	ilde{z}$), and the selection of preferred wavevectors ($q_c$) leading to stripe patterns.

main_assumptions: The analysis utilizes the Stokesian limit (neglecting inertia) and makes approximations regarding the relevance of nonlinear terms in the RG sense.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate steady-state anisotropic patterns under varying parameters, show the stability profile of the dispersion relation $\lambda_h(q)$, and demonstrate the robustness of the patterned phase against initial conditions and the suppression of patterns by increasing $|\lambda|$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the long-wavelength, statistically flat regime (emergent symmetry) to analyzing the intermediate-scale dynamics governed by KPZ-like equations. It then uses linear stability analysis to predict pattern formation at finite wavevectors, concluding with numerical verification of pattern robustness and the role of nonlinearity in suppressing these patterns.
why_interesting: The study of non-equilibrium pattern formation and symmetry breaking in active matter systems provides theoretical frameworks applicable to complex many-body dynamics, which shares conceptual links with driven quantum many-body systems.
